title: WPSS/936/2013 of Rahul Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 936 of 2013
Rahul Singh Ö Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Present: Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. N.P. Shah, Brief Holder, present for the
State/respondent no.1.
 Mr. Rakesh Thapaliyal, Advocate, present for the
respondent no.2.
 Mr. A.M. Saklani, Advocate, present for the respondent nos.
3 & 5.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner before this Court was a candidate
in the Combined Selection Examination-2011, for filling up
of Group ìCî posts. Petitioner applied for the post of Cane
Supervisor as well as Government Milk Supervisor. This
selection was being made by a body, known as
ìUttarakhand Technical Education Boardî. Petitioner has
applied in the said examination as an OBC candidate,
though there was no post for the candidates belonging to
OBC category. Apart from that, he also applied under the
quota reserved for ìphysically challengedî, persons, for
which he has relevant documents to support his claim.
2. Since, there was no post for OBC category
candidates; petitioner could have only competed as a
ìgeneral categoryî candidate in which he has not been
selected. Petitioner has not been selected under the
ìphysically handicappedî category as well. However, under
the ìphysically challengedî category, other candidates who
got less marks than the petitioner have been selected.
3. Aggrieved, the petitioner has filed present writ
petition.

2
4. The case of the respondents nos. 3, 4 & 5 is that
they belong to general category and since there was no
reservation for OBC, logically there was no reservation for
ìphysically handicappedî OBC candidates as these
reservations are horizontal.
3. This contention of the respondents nos. 3, 4 & 5
is not correct. Petitioner is a ìphysically challengedî
candidate, who has secured 24.75 marks as against the
private respondent nos. 3, 4 & 5, who have got 24.25, 24
and 23.75 marks respectively. Admittedly, therefore, the
petitioner secured higher marks than the private
respondents. Therefore, the petitioner has better claim
than any of the private respondents.
4. In view thereof, the writ petition is allowed. A
mandamus is issued to the respondent nos. 1 & 2/State
authorities to recommend the name of the petitioner for
appointment under the ìphysically handicappedî quota,
unless there is some other disqualification attached to the
candidature of the petitioner and consequently the
respondent no.1 & 2 shall pass appropriate order. It is,
however, made clear that since admittedly there are many
other vacancies for Cane Supervisor available with the
State, under the ìfreedom fighterî category and one under
the ìsports category,î (which have remained unfilled), for
which respondents nos. 1 & 2 could not get eligible
candidates, the petitionerís candidature firstly be adjusted
against these vacancies, as there is no provision for
carrying forward vacancies of ìfreedom fighterî or ìsports
personsî category for the next year. If the respondents
cannot adjust the petitioner under these categories, they

3
must assign reasons and then shall the candidature of the
private respondents be disturbed.
5. Let the needful be done within a period of six
weeks from the date of production of certified copy of this
order.
6. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 27.04.2015
Nitesh
